newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES SOFTER IN LIQUID MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES SOFTER IN LIQUID MARKET.

text.p: Zimbabwe's money market continued liquid on Thursday with short-term trading rates quoted mixed in quiet trade, dealers said.
The central Reserve Bank, anticipating a market surplus at the end of the day, auctioned Z$750 million worth of 91-day treasury bills at 17.38 percent, down from 17.50 percent previously.
Treasury bills were being sold in the secondary market at 17.25 percent while call money edged up to 17.25 percent from 17 percent.
NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were quoted softer at 18 from 18.25 percent but their buying rated edged up to 17.75 from 17.50 percent.
Bankers acceptances were quoted at 17.75 and 17.35 percent (buying and selling respectively) from Wednesday's 18 and 17 percent.
The central bank indicated a market surplus of Z$49 million at the close of Wednesday trade, down from Tuesday's Z$141 million.
